messages:
sara: Announcing rollout plan for the Operator Privilege Separation + Immutable Config policy for Private installs. Goal: improve least-privilege posture and produce auditable config artifacts for SOC2. Docs and a migration checklist are live in staging.

kevin: Quick recap: operator processes will be split into control-plane-only and runtime-only roles. Customers can opt into enforcement (recommended) or run permissive mode to get reports first.

security: Important compliance note: when enforcement=strict we will require a signed config bundle (SHA256) stored in customer audit logs. This is required for attestation evidence.

ops-bot: Docs staged: private/operator-privsep/readme.md (v0.8) by sara

sara: Sample config snippet we'll ship for on-prem teams:

```yaml
operator_policy:
  mode: permissive  # permissive | strict | off
  signed_bundle_required: true
  allowed_operator_users: ["ops-team", "redwood-agent"]
```

support: Action item: add KB article with migration steps and common troubleshooting (permissions denied on deploy, missing signatures). Tag support routing `privsep-operator`.

wayne: Migration tool will produce a report: permissions-report.csv + unsigned-bundles.csv. We'll run dry-runs against a set of beta customers next week.

kevin: Rollout timeline: internal verification (this week), invite-only beta (week of Apr 12), opt-in public beta (Apr 26), enforcement GA (May 17). No forced enforcement for existing customers without explicit opt-in.

security: Also adding recommended minimal IAM roles and an example attestation template to the docs. Keep PII out of attestations.

sara: Thanks all. Please review the staging doc and drop comments. I'll coordinate customer comms after beta reports look clean. :spiral_calendar:
